title: Where to live in Alanya: the areas compared | Assel Usmanova
desc: Alanya's areas in plain words: Mahmutlar, Oba, Kestel, Tosmur, Avsallar, the centre and Gazipasa. Who each one suits and what to look at.
lead: Alanya stretches along the sea for almost 70 km, and its areas differ a lot. A short note on each: who it suits and what to look for.

cards.name: City centre and Cleopatra
cards.who: No car needed, the city at your door
cards.p: Cleopatra Beach, the promenade, cafés and shops within walking distance. Few new-builds, higher prices, noisier in summer.

cards.name: Oba
cards.p: A green, quiet area next to the centre. Schools, clinics, a market, and many Russian-speaking families.

cards.name: Tosmur
cards.p: By the Dim River, quieter than Oba. New complexes, a few minutes to Kestel beach.

cards.name: Kestel
cards.p: Complexes right on the seafront and a long beach. Fewer shops than in Oba, but the centre is close.

cards.name: Mahmutlar
cards.p: A large area with its own infrastructure and a long promenade. Many complexes with pools, prices lower than in the centre.

cards.name: Kargicak
cards.p: The hills beyond Mahmutlar: sea views, villas and small complexes. Easier with a car.

cards.name: Cikcilli
cards.who: Close to the city, new buildings
cards.p: A slope above the centre. New complexes, close to the centre and the beach, but uphill in places.

cards.name: Avsallar and Konakli
cards.p: West of the centre, near Incekum beach. Calmer, with many affordable new-builds.

cards.name: Gazipasa
cards.p: 40 km to the east, next to Gazipasa Airport. The most affordable prices, quiet, and the area is growing.

items: Living year-round: look at schools, clinics and shops nearby. Oba, Tosmur and Mahmutlar are chosen most often.
Renting out: distance to the sea and a 1+1 layout matter more. It is the easiest to rent out.
Without a car: the centre, Oba, Mahmutlar. In Kargicak and on the hills it's hard without a car.
Come and stay in the area for a couple of days before buying. If you're not in Türkiye, I'll show you the area by video call.

title: Investing in Alanya property: rental, resale, costs | Assel Usmanova
desc: How people earn on apartments in Alanya: long-term and short-term rental, buying during construction. What to look at and which costs to plan for.
h1: An apartment in Alanya as an investment
lead: An apartment by the sea can bring income, but only if it's chosen well. Three ways and what matters in each.

cards.p: Steady income all year and less hassle. Tenants look for homes near schools, shops and transport.
Income is higher in summer and lower in winter. You need a management company and a short-term rental permit: without it, daily rentals are not allowed in Türkiye.
The price is lower than for a finished building. By completion the price usually rises, but there is a risk of delays.

items: Distance to the sea and layout: a 1+1 by the sea rents and sells fastest.
Aidat: the monthly fee for maintaining the complex. It takes part of the rental income.
The developer: which buildings they have completed, and whether on time.
Documents: the occupancy permit (iskan) and the TAPU, i.e. the title deed.
Property valuation report: mandatory for foreigners.
If you rent out: tax on rental income.

title: Turkish citizenship by buying property in Alanya | Assel Usmanova
desc: How to get Turkish citizenship through a property purchase: conditions, who gets a passport, the steps and how it differs from a residence permit.
lead: Buying property from a certain amount gives the whole family the right to a Turkish passport. Here is how it works.

cards.p: It can be one apartment or several; their values add up. The value is confirmed by an official appraiser.
A no-sale restriction for three years is recorded in the TAPU. You can still rent the apartment out.
The applicant, their spouse and children under 18 receive passports.

items: Choosing properties for the required amount.
Valuation, purchase and TAPU with the no-sale note.
A property-based residence permit is also possible with a cheaper apartment. It has to be renewed.
Citizenship gives a passport for good, but requires a purchase from $400,000 and a 3-year no-sale restriction.
